fix: Add autofillHints to password field for Android autofill support

Adds autofillHints property with AutofillHints.password to the password
TextFormField in PasswordField widget. This enables password managers 
like Bitwarden to properly detect and autofill password fields on 
Android devices.

Without this hint, the Android autofill framework cannot identify the
field as a password input, preventing password managers from offering
autofill suggestions.

Changes:
- Added autofillHints: const [AutofillHints.password] to TextFormField
  in lib/widgets/auth/password_field.dart

Tested on Android with Bitwarden password manager.

Fix crash when copying a log with no hydrated exercise

Log.exerciseObj was declared late and is only ever assigned when
hydrating the logs of a routine's sessions. Logs read from the database
are built through drift's row class and only carry exerciseId, so
copyWith threw a LateInitializationError when it unconditionally read
the field. Copying a past log in gym mode does exactly that.

Make the field nullable behind a getter that throws a descriptive error,
add exerciseObjOrNull for callers that legitimately handle logs straight
from the database, and only carry the exercise over when there is one.

Hydrating the exercise in watchLogsByExerciseDrift instead would mean
joining its translations, images, muscles and equipment for every log,
which most callers don't need.

The log page tests mocked the query with the test routine's logs, which
are hydrated, which is why this was never caught. They now return logs
without an exercise, like the real query does.

fix(auth): do not await PowerSync disconnect during session clear

A rejected refresh token runs clearSessionOnly inside the single-flight
refresh future. PowerSync's disconnect can block on an in-flight sync
fetch that is itself awaiting that same refresh future through
AuthHttpClient's pre-emptive refresh, closing a three-party cycle
(refresh -> disconnect -> sync fetch -> refresh) that permanently wedges
every authenticated request behind the never-completing refresh. The
session-expired message never appears because it is sequenced after the
hanging call, and an app restart re-triggers the same rejected refresh
during startup revalidation, so the deadlock re-forms immediately.

On the keep-data path the DB is not wiped, so there is no re-attach race
to guard against; the disconnect is only a courtesy stop of the sync
loop and is now fire-and-forget. The wipe path (explicit logout) keeps
its ordering. The disconnect hook is injectable for tests because
PowerSyncDatabase is a base class that cannot be faked.

fix(core): make UI side effects and provider reads safe during build

Errors handled while the widget tree is building crashed or wedged the
app in three related ways:

- FlutterError.onError showed dialogs and snackbars synchronously.
  Pushing a route mid-build trips the navigator's !_debugLocked
  assertion, and because the one-dialog guard was set before showDialog
  threw, its release never attached: every later error dialog was then
  silently suppressed while nothing was on screen, leaving a blank,
  unresponsive app until restart. Snackbars crashed outright via the
  messenger's setState.
- The sync status and barcode dialogs did ref.read inside their route
  builders, which run during build. With the provider chain dirty (any
  token refresh dirties wgerBase -> auth), the read flushed it there and
  Riverpod scheduled a scope refresh mid-build. The barcode builder also
  created its search future inline, re-firing the search on every dialog
  rebuild.
- Provider create bodies that widgets watch during build read providers
  synchronously: the dashboard's routine hydration chain crashed on cold
  start right after a token refresh, and TrophyStateNotifier.build()
  has the same shape in the post-login window, where invalidation order
  left networkStatusProvider dirty while its dependents rebuilt.

lib/core/build_safety.dart adds the two idioms as helpers: runAfterFrame
defers UI side effects past the build phase, yieldPastBuild yields
provider create bodies past their synchronous phase (a microtask, not a
timer, since widget tests assert !timersPending at teardown). The error
dialog guard is released when the context is gone or the push fails, the
snackbar helpers re-resolve the messenger inside the callback, the
dialog builders snapshot their providers in the tap handler, and
post-login invalidation runs leaf-first. Regression tests cover each
shape.
